'''John Antonio Nettles-Abraham'''<ref name=Athletic>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6613777/2025/09/25/john-abraham-nfl-falcons-jets-cardinals|title=Ex-NFL sack master John Abraham paid a steep price for success. He's still recovering|author1=Dan Pompei|publisher=[[The Athletic]]|date=September 25, 2025}}</ref> (born May 6, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] and [[linebacker]] for 15 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]], and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the first round of the [[2000 NFL draft]]. '''Joseph Elleweyn Thomas''' (born August 29, 1980) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[cornerback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the third round of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Montana State University – Bozeman|Montana State]].

Thomas was also a member of the [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Edmonton Eskimos]], [[Miami Dolphins]] and [[Oakland Raiders]].

The past few years, Thomas was the head football coach at [[Ballard High School (Seattle, Washington)|Ballard High School]] in Seattle, Washington. However, he decided to become the head coach at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle.

'''Joffrey Roy Reynolds''' (born November 26, 1979) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[running back]]. He played eight years for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and became Calgary's all-time leading [[Rush (gridiron football)|rusher]] with 9,213 yards.<ref name="Calgary release">{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/article/stamps-release-franchise-rushing-leader-reynolds |title=Stamps release franchise rushing leader Reynolds |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=January 23, 2013 |access-date=October 29, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720050935/http://www.cfl.ca/article/stamps-release-franchise-rushing-leader-reynolds |archive-date=July 20, 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref> For six consecutive years Reynolds rushed for over 1,000 yards. He was named a CFL All-Star four times and won a [[Grey Cup]] championship with the Stampeders in [[96th Grey Cup|2008]]. He attended the [[University of Houston]]. Reynolds also played for the [[St. Louis Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

'''John Earl Armstrong''' (born July 7, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] with the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in 1987.

Armstrong played multiple positions for the [[Bruce, Mississippi|Bruce High School]] football team, as well as [[basketball]] and [[track and field]], before going on to [[Northwest Mississippi Community College]].<ref name="John Armstrong">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/clarion-ledger-john-armstrong/128493095/|title=John Armstrong|page=37|work=[[The Clarion-Ledger]]|author=Baker, Lee|via=Newspapers.com|date=November 4, 1985|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> There he earned [[junior college]] [[All-America]]n status as the team won a national junior college championship.<ref name="Happy returns">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch-happy-returns/128492676/|title=Happy returns|page=27|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|author=O'Connor, John|via=Newspapers.com|date=October 26, 1985|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Armstrong leads in returns">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch-armstrong-leads/128492854/|title=Armstrong leads in returns|page=32|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|author=O'Connor, John|via=Newspapers.com|date=October 26, 1985|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="John Armstrong"/>

After two years, he joined the football team of the [[University of Richmond]], where he majored in [[physical education]].<ref name="Happy returns"/><ref name="University of Richmond Player of the Week">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch-university-of-ri/128492781/|title=University of Richmond Player of the Week|page=52|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=September 26, 1985|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> He became a starting [[cornerback]] during his senior year in 1985 and ranked among the top [[Punt (gridiron football)#Return|punt]] and [[Kickoff (gridiron football)#Return|kickoff returners]] in the country.<ref name="Armstrong leads in returns"/>

In the [[1986 NFL draft]], Armstrong was drafted by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the 11th round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Team-by-team draft picks">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-south-bend-tribune-team-by-team-draf/128494446/|title=Team-by-team draft picks|page=12|work=[[South Bend Tribune]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=April 30, 1986|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> He was released from the team on August 19.<ref name="Vikings cut 6, waive 10">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-winona-daily-news-vikings-cut-6-wai/128494582/|title=Vikings cut 6, waive 10|page=9|work=[[Winona Daily News]]|author=[[The Associated Press]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=August 20, 1986|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> Armstrong signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 1987 and played with the team in the [[NFL preseason|preseason]], but was placed on [[Waivers (American football)|waivers]] on August 31.<ref name="Ed Luther Has Long Second Half">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-ed-luther-has-long/128493378/|title=Ed Luther Has Long Second Half|page=76|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|author=Roberts, Rich|via=Newspapers.com|date=August 23, 1987|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Transactions">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette-transactions/128493419/|title=Transactions|page=27|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=September 1, 1987|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref>

He rejoined the team as a non-roster [[replacement player]] during the [[1987 NFL season#The NFLPA strike|1987 National Football League Players Association strike]]. On September 23, he was interrogated and harassed at a hotel by striking Bills players, including [[Greg Bell (running back, born 1962)|Greg Bell]], [[Joe Devlin (American football)|Joe Devlin]], [[Sean McNanie]] and [[Fred Smerlas]], for playing as a [[strikebreaker]].<ref name="Confrontation spices strike">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/democrat-and-chronicle-confrontation-spi/128493610/|title=Confrontation spices strike|page=33|work=[[Democrat and Chronicle]]|author=Pitoniak, Scott|via=Newspapers.com|date=September 24, 1987|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> He appeared in three games for Buffalo, starting two.<ref name="John Armstrong statistics at Pro-Football-Reference">{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsJo21.htm|title=John Armstrong statistics at Pro-Football-Reference|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref> He signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in 1988, but was cut in August before the season began.<ref name="Falcons Cuts">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-constitution-falcons-cuts/128494035/|title=Falcons Cuts|page=65|work=[[The Atlanta Constitution|The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=August 30, 1988|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Falcons">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-constitution-falcons/128494061/|title=Falcons|page=70|work=[[The Atlanta Constitution|The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=August 30, 1988|access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref>

Arnold was born in [[Shizuoka (city)|Shizuoka]], Japan, the son of an [[United States Armed Forces|American serviceman]] and Japanese woman.<ref name="State grads go to NFL">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-state-grads-go-to-nfl/128611069/|title=State grads go to NFL|page=20|work=[[The News Tribune]]|author=Luebker, Earl|via=Newspapers.com|date=September 16, 1981|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Detroit has a new model but it stalls">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-journal-detroit-has-a-new-mo/128610773/|title=Detroit has a new model but it stalls|page=43|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|The Atlanta Journal]]|author=[[Furman Bisher]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=October 6, 1980|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref> Arnold played [[college football]] at the [[University of Wyoming]]. Before his junior season with the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Cowboys]], three fingers on his left hand were severed after an accident during his offseason job at a lumber processing plant in [[Seattle, Washington]], on July 27, 1977. His fingers were sewed back on, but Arnold missed the 1977 season.<ref name="Pokes lose Arnold">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/casper-star-tribune-pokes-lose-arnold/128611865/|title=Pokes lose Arnold|page=9|work=[[Casper Star-Tribune]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=July 26, 1977|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Poke plies positive power">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/casper-star-tribune-poke-plies-positive/128612775/|title=Poke plies positive power|page=17|work=[[Casper Star-Tribune]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=May 9, 1978|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Wyoming grid coach makes no predictions">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-albuquerque-tribune-wyoming-grid-coa/128613002/|title=Wyoming grid coach makes no predictions|page=50|work=[[The Albuquerque Tribune]]|author=Mossman, John|via=Newspapers.com|date=August 31, 1978|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref>

He signed a two-year contract with the [[Detroit Lions]] in the spring of 1979.<ref name="Detroit signs John Arnold">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-detroit-signs-john-arno/128613163/|title=Detroit signs John Arnold|page=22|work=[[The News Tribune]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=June 6, 1979|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Jack Arnold is back with Detroit Lions">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/standard-speaker-jack-arnold-is-back-wit/128609870/|title=State grads go to NFL|page=23|work=Standard-Speaker|author=[[Associated Press]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=November 1, 1979|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref> He was released before the start of the regular season. By October 31, he was re-signed by the team after an injury to fellow [[wide receiver]] [[Luther Blue]].<ref name="Jack Arnold is back with Detroit Lions"/> He was [[waivers (sports)|waived]] by Detroit before the 1981 season began.<ref name="Transactions">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-worth-star-telegram-transactions/128611056/|title=Transactions|page=32|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|via=Newspapers.com|date=September 1, 1981|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref>

In March 1982, Arnold was awarded $400,000 in damages by a [[superior court]] for the injuries he sustained in 1977 that resulted in the loss of his fingers, with Arnold's attorneys arguing the injury cost the player a high spot in the [[National Football League Draft]].<ref name="Football player scores $400,000 for hand injury suffered in plywood mill">{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-football-player-scores/128613472/|title=Football player scores $400,000 for hand injury suffered in plywood mill|page=3|work=[[The News Tribune]]|author=Churchill, Marlowe|via=Newspapers.com|date=March 12, 1982|access-date=July 21, 2023}}</ref>
